title: Reported Speech Quiz 1
description: Move the verb one step back, change the modal verbs, and choose between said and told.
topic: Reported statements: tenses, say and tell
instructions: Reported Speech: Reported statements: tenses, say and tell.
Use the standard rule: the reporting verb is in the past and the situation is over, unless a question says otherwise.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Report this: 'I am tired,' she said.
options: She said she had been tired.
questions.explanation: The present simple becomes the past simple, and I becomes she. Watch out: is would keep the present, and had been tired would go back two steps.

questions.question: Report this: 'We have finished,' they said.
questions.explanation: The present perfect becomes the past perfect, and we becomes they. Watch out: the pronoun we cannot stay when the speakers are they.

questions.question: 'I can drive, and I will help,' he said. → He said that he {{1}} drive and {{2}} help.
questions.explanation: Can becomes could and will becomes would. Watch out: both modals move back together.

questions.question: 'I may be late,' he said. → He said he {{1}} be late.
questions.explanation: May becomes might in reported speech. Watch out: may would stay in the present.

questions.question: 'I am reading,' she said. → She said she had been reading.
questions.explanation: The present continuous becomes the past continuous: She said she was reading. Watch out: had been reading is two steps back.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: She said me she was ill.
She told to me she was ill.
She told me she was ill.
questions.explanation: Told needs a person straight after it: She told me she was ill. Watch out: said me and told to me are both wrong.

questions.question: Choose the reported verb form.
questions.explanation: Each verb goes one step back. Watch out: will becomes would, and can becomes could.

questions.question: Match each modal verb with its reported form.
questions.explanation: Each modal has its own partner. Watch out: must becomes had to, not musted.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The subject comes first, then the reporting verb, then the clause. Watch out: the clause keeps statement order.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: She told me she has finished.
He said me he was late.
She told us she had lost her keys.
questions.explanation: A past reporting verb needs the backshift, and told needs a person. Watch out: has finished and said me break these rules.

questions.question: Which report is correct? 'I am tired,' she says.
options: She says she had been tired.
She says she would be tired.
questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the present, the tense does not change: She says she is tired. Watch out: backshift only follows a past reporting verb.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: She said me that she was tired.
accepted: She told me that she was tired.
She told me that she was tired
She told me she was tired.
She told me she was tired
She said that she was tired.
She said that she was tired
She said to me that she was tired.
She said to me that she was tired
She said to me she was tired.
She said to me she was tired
questions.explanation: Said has no person after it, so use told me or remove me: She told me that she was tired. Watch out: said to me is possible, but said me is not.
